laws.related: Lumen.MineralSpeciation (LAW-002); SI.ZnAvailability (LAW-003); Transit; Dilution; LAW-008 framework
laws.law: Under fibre-rich whole-plant diets, measured apparent fractional absorption of Ca, Mg, P, K tends to fall.
laws.bound: Example (Southgate 1987 via H89): fibre ~9.3→21.5 g/d, Ca fraction ~0.26→0.19; Mg/P/K parallel. Provisional; not pure isolated-fibre.
laws.conditions: Fibre from unrefined sources; phytate co-travel; absolute mineral intake may rise so grams absorbed partly compensate.
laws.relation: fibre_rich_matrix NARROWS_BOUND fractional_absorption(Ca|Mg|P|K)
laws.note: Meter reading of several mechanisms. Atomic split: see reformulations/LAW-001-fibre-mineral-fraction.md (L-001a–f).

laws.related: LAW-001 composite; LAW-003 ratio bound; LAW-041 iron redox; Biotransformation (microbial phytase)
laws.law: Phytate binds divalent minerals into insoluble complexes until phytase hydrolyses it and frees them.
laws.gate: none (monoferric phytate partial exception — not total lock)
laws.bound: Qualitative free-ion reduction; dose–response locked as ratio in LAW-003. Monoferric phytate <5% of wheat-bran phytate (Morris & Ellis).
laws.conditions: Co-present phytate in meal lumen; phytase from food processing, microbes, or host context; divalent mineral load.
laws.relation: phytate NARROWS_BOUND free_mineral_for_uptake; phytase EXPANDS_BOUND free_mineral
laws.note: True governing mechanism for much of LAW-001's effect.

laws.related: LAW-002 chelation; LAW-005 meat factor; LAW-010 bran selectivity
laws.law: Dietary phytate:Zn molar ratio predicts Zn bioavailability risk; phytate×Ca:Zn is a sharper predictor.
laws.bound: phytate:Zn ≳ ~10 elevated risk; phytate×Ca:Zn ~0.51 cited as upper edge of normal range in Harland vegetarians.
laws.conditions: Habitual co-intake of phytate, Ca, Zn; fermentation/phytase lowers effective phytate; population diet pattern.
laws.relation: phytate:Zn_ratio NARROWS_BOUND Zn_bioavailability (step-like risk)
laws.note: Standout computable Vol-I law — promote early to print.

laws.related: LAW-006 tannin inhibitor; LAW-012 Fenton (same ascorbate, opposite context); LAW-041 redox gate
laws.law: Co-ingested ascorbic acid increases non-haem Fe absorption and can overcome inhibitors such as tea tannin.
laws.bound: Tea 3.8%→2.1% Fe abs.; ascorbate ~10× rise and cancels tea inhibition (Derman 1977); orange juice ~2× (Rossander).
laws.conditions: Ascorbate in the SAME meal as non-haem Fe (L3 event); applies to non-haem not haem Fe.
laws.relation: ascorbate EXPANDS_BOUND nonhaem_Fe_absorption; can override tannin NARROWS_BOUND
laws.note: Flagship EXPANDS_BOUND. Context-flips with LAW-012.

laws.related: LAW-004 ascorbate (independent enhancer); LAW-003 Zn; LAW-006 tannin
laws.law: Animal tissue co-ingested with plant meals increases absorption of non-haem Fe (and Zn).
laws.bound: ~2× (50 g meat / 100 g fish / 150 g papaya-as-C); fruit+meat ~5× (Hallberg); animal protein+milk ↑ Zn from wholemeal bread.
laws.conditions: Same-meal animal tissue (L3); partly independent of ascorbate path.
laws.relation: meat_fish_factor EXPANDS_BOUND nonhaem_Fe_and_Zn_absorption
laws.note: Interaction term, not additive food score.

laws.related: LAW-004 ascorbate rescue; casein rescue; LAW-002 chelation family

laws.relation: tannin NARROWS_BOUND nonhaem_Fe; casein EXPANDS_BOUND (partial rescue); ascorbate EXPANDS_BOUND (stronger rescue)

laws.law: Free Fe²⁺ + H₂O₂ generates •OH (Fenton); reducing agents regenerate Fe²⁺ catalytic cycle; damage local to site of production.
laws.gate: none for reaction existence; binding proteins constrain free pool (physiological containment)

laws.conditions: Non-protein-bound Fe only; reducing agents (superoxide, ascorbate); H₂O₂ present.

laws.relation: cofactor_i EXPANDS_BOUND network_capacity; missing_cofactor_i NARROWS_BOUND network_capacity
laws.note: Network property, not single-nutrient score.
